In the case on hand, we find clear and spe- cific averments not in the complaint but also in the statutory notice issued to the respondent." It is thereafter that in the decision in S.P. Mani's case (supra) in paragraph 47 (a) it was held that the primary responsibility of the complainant is to make specific averments in the complaint so as to make the accused vicariously liable. In the decision in Anita Malhotra's case (supra) in paragraph 22 it was held thus:- "22. This Court has repeatedly held that in case of a Director, the complaint should specifically spell out how and in what manner the Director Crl. and mere bald statement that he or she was in charge of and was responsible to the company for con- duct of its business is not sufficient. (Vide Na- tional Small Industries Corpn. Ltd. v. Harmeet Singh Paintal). 15. Paragraph 19 of the Ashok Shewakramani's case (supra) is also relevant for the purpose of the case and it, in so far as relevant, reads thus: "19. Thus, the settled position of law is that for a Director of a Crl.
